experiment: E9: the deployed configuration for seven days on the lab installation (Home Assistant 2026.7.4, virtual devices, purge_keep_days 30, auto_purge on): two monitors (direct read and copy), both stable columns with coverage, Ed25519 record signatures, escrow, name-map digest, per-row keylog binding and the full-history initial seal; each with its own linked anchor (append key, separate operator key, tagged replies) and a head witness outside Docker's VM; the deployment's own nightly purges under operator-signed PURGE markers, one planned restart, one restore, one benign rename, the person re-link attack and its benign counterpart, and one attack batch a day
registered_before: any event of the main run (tag e9_main); smoke runs on the scratch stack (prefix e9s-, outputs outside exp/out) precede it and are not results
approval: PI 2026-10-09: '7 days (Recommended)'; code changes and smaller additions 'You decide what is the best for s&p' (drafts/round13/E9_DESIGN.md)

schedule.end_utc: 2026-10-18T12:01:00Z (end event; the freeze and scoring follow)
schedule.condition: starts only if the part-A code is reviewed, both test suites pass, a smoke run on the final code exits 0 and scores; otherwise the start moves by whole days (HPR_E9_START) and this file is re-issued before any event
schedule.day_window: day d = [START + (d-1) x 24 h, START + d x 24 h), 12:00 UTC to 12:00 UTC

daily_utc.14:00: attack batch (rooms rotate porch, hallway, kitchen)
daily_utc.03:40: sleep guard (restart the hub if its 04:12 purge timer is more than 30 s late)
daily_utc.04:07:00 / 04:10:00: operator PURGE marker: the issuer container starts / posts to both anchors (retried until 04:12:00, when the hub purges)

special.2026-10-13 17:00: name-map session, in this order: benign entity rename (light.porch_light -> 'Porch lamp') under a RENAME marker; the person re-link as a MOVE (hpr has one household account): the household account's user_id moves from its person to the person without an account ('Jordan Rivera (household)', created at setup), two person_update calls (unlink P1, link P2), declared under RENAME markers for every intermediate name-map state, and moved back (unlink P2, link P1) the same way; then the ATTACK, the same move with no marker and no recorder row written, held 180 s (the verifier consumes a RENAME marker at its first matching transition and counts a duplicated marker once, so the earlier declared move cannot excuse it); its declared move back. The run log names the mode used (move; a swap of two persons' accounts only on a hub without the account-less person)
special.2026-10-14 20:00 / 20:30: backup of the recorder: a consistent SQLite copy wrapped in Home Assistant's backup format and hashed, HELD OUTSIDE THE HUB (run directory, read-only) / an operator RESTORE marker (backup_wm, archive and database sha256 signed into it); 30 s later the hub is STOPPED, the archive and .HA_RESTORE (restore_database=true, restore_homeassistant=false) are placed, the archive's copy in the hub is read back and must match the signed sha256 (else no restore), the hub is started and Home Assistant's own start-up restore runs; once its log says 'Restore complete' and the operator reads the restored recorder's watermark from outside the hub, an operator RESTORE_DONE marker (rig.marker_issuer.restore_done_marker: restore_nonce, restore_sha256 = the SHA-256 of the RESTORE marker's canonical JSON, post_restart_wm, hub_started_ts H = the restored hub's container start) is issued and anchored within 600 s of the RESTORE marker (review re-check N1, E9_IMPL_NOTES.md 12.1)

notes: 2026-10-11 is the second Sunday of the month: the 04:12 purge that day also repacks (auto_repack); it falls before START. No second Sunday falls inside the run.
Every wait is on the wall clock; no hub restart in [03:50, 04:45) UTC.

parameters.verifier_purge_tol_basis: tol > 0 is required: Home Assistant's own cutoff (its fire time minus keep) lies in [c0, c0 + tol] with c0 = scheduled - keep; with tol = 0 a purge that fires a fraction of a second late leaves unexcused deletions (E9_IMPL_NOTES.md 10.2); 60 s as in E2
parameters.verifier_purge_seen_slack_basis: e7_verify.py PURGE_SEEN_SLACK_S (review R7): a removed row counts as purged only if first observed by a poll that copied at or before scheduled + tol + 60 s
parameters.verifier_restore_done_max_basis: review N1 / re-check 2: a RESTORE marker excuses nothing unless its operator-signed RESTORE_DONE is issued and anchored within this after the RESTORE marker's issued_ts. Measured in the final smoke run on the frozen code: 82.5 s (anchor-direct 82.50 s, anchor-copy 82.53 s, chain receive times; final smoke e9s_final, 2026-10-10 07:18:08 to 07:19:31 UTC: hub stop, archive placed and its copy checked, start, Home Assistant's restore, the restored watermark read outside the hub, RESTORE_DONE issued; H 35.2 s and the first poll reading the restored recorder 37.8 s after the RESTORE marker) from the RESTORE marker to the anchored RESTORE_DONE (both anchors). The reviewer estimated the worst case at about 300 s; smoke 3 (old sequence, no RESTORE_DONE) took 78 s from the RESTORE marker to the operator's post-restart observation; the hub stop, the archive check and up to a minute of Docker latency per container start are inside 600 s
parameters.restore_done_validity_rule: scorer (e9_score.py restore_done_check), review re-check 2: every anchored, operator-signed RESTORE_DONE must carry hub_started_ts H and a post_restart_wm consistent with the restored recorder observed afterwards (the first snapshot after the RESTORE_DONE was anchored): post_restart_wm >= the RESTORE marker's signed backup_wm in each table, the recorder holds the keys up to post_restart_wm, and no row with a key above backup_wm was written before H. A RESTORE_DONE lacking H or failing a check is reported INVALID and the restore it closes counts as not excused (its RESTORE-excused segments are counted as unexcused). Without H the verifier would excuse a deletion between the restart and the first post-restore poll (reproduced by the reviewer); the harness always sends H
parameters.verifier_restore_max_age_basis: a RESTORE marker with issued_ts - restore_point_ts above it is rejected (review m2); E9's restore marker comes about 30 min after its backup
parameters.initial_seal: M-direct first; M-copy only after M-direct's history is anchored (its poll counter 6 polls past its first record); at most 5,400 s each, else the run does not start
parameters.monitor_env_both: HOMEPROV_SCHEME=stable HOMEPROV_COVERAGE=1 HOMEPROV_ESCROW_DIR HOMEPROV_COST_LOG HOMEPROV_SIGN_KEY HOMEPROV_REPLY_TAGS=1 HOMEPROV_NAMEMAP_DIR=/cfg/.storage HOMEPROV_SINCE=0 HOMEPROV_ROWBIND=1 HOMEPROV_KEYLOG_REWIND=1 HOMEPROV_PERIOD=5
parameters.quick_check_every_smoke_only: the smoke runs use M-direct 12 (once a minute) so the hourly path is exercised several times; the real run keeps 720 (its preflight refuses any other value). Final smoke: M-direct quick_check due at 64 of 769 polls, snapshot stage median 242.6 ms when due against 1.3 ms otherwise; M-copy at every poll (705), median 124.3 ms; no quick_check failure and no unobservable poll in either
parameters.quick_check_every_basis: lead decision 2026-10-10. M-direct 720 (once an hour at 5 s polls): in direct mode quick_check reads the whole live database inside the read transaction and holds off a checkpoint's backfill for that long (E9_IMPL_NOTES.md section 9 item 4), while the per-poll consistency check (WAL salts, checkpoint sequence, change counter; read_raced) catches a torn read at every poll. M-copy 1 (every poll, as E8's copy path did). C1 measured direct mode at both cadences (E9_PRE_NOTES.md) and the final direct-mode re-run measures both again. The run's preflight refuses other values and logs each container's own setting
parameters.verifier: exp/stages/e7_verify.py verify --scheme stable --late-bound 30 --gap-s 30 --sign-pubkey <monitor> --escrow <monitor escrow> --operator-pubkey <operator> --purge-keep-s 2592000 --purge-tol-s 60 --restore-tol-s 30 --restore-max-age-s 86400 --restore-done-max-s 600 [--namemap-storage <sanitized storage>, last day] [--trials <day reports>]; each day again with --no-rowbind (suspects without the per-row binding, which then is used nowhere); each night's post-purge snapshot again with --no-purge-disconnect (the round-12 rule, for comparison)
parameters.scorer_jobs_basis: E9_VERIFY_JOBS=2 verifications in parallel, on the host after the freeze (not in Docker's VM). Measured with the indexed escrow on the E8 recorder history (E9_IMPL_NOTES.md 11.2): a day window 64.8 s, 1.17 GB resident (1.36 GB peak footprint); a whole-history window 140.3 s, 1.81 GB resident (2.99 GB footprint): two jobs need at most about 6 GB of the Mac's 24 GB beside the Docker VM. Final smoke (full seed, 2.66 GB escrow per monitor): 18 verifications with 2 jobs in 877 s (day windows 64-72 s, whole-history windows 151-160 s)
parameters.settings_checked: against drafts/round13/E9_IMPL_NOTES.md section 8 (2026-10-10, part A final pending its re-check); --final re-hashes every file

components.homeprov_e6: setup (persons) and the name-map session only; outside the repository, never released

arms.order_per_batch: homeprov_ec (PU, PSR), then homeprov_e7 (INS-L, BD-S); one hub restart switches each on (exactly one listed in configuration.yaml), one more switches both off
arms.scored_by: both monitors (each trial counts once per monitor)

benign_events.setup: before START: `person:` added to configuration.yaml, one person per household account (active, not system-generated) that has none, and one person without an account, 'Jordan Rivera (household)' (user_id null), the person move's target (homeprov_e6 person_create, the call the person/create websocket handler makes); no account and no token is created

primary.unexcused_untouched: per day and monitor: attributable violations on UNTOUCHED segments that the verifier does not excuse under an operator-signed marker, at one-second, minute and hour granularity, with the untouched anchored segments as denominators (paper's counting rule: a segment is touched when it holds a row any trial wrote, edited or named)
primary.purge: per night and monitor: the verifier's NEW attributable violations between the 03:55 and 04:45 snapshots over the historical window (segments sealed by the full-history initial seal), split into excused (segment older than c0 gone, tolerance band [c0, c0 + tol], purge disconnect: count, seconds, rows; and keylog ranges purged or disconnected) and unexcused, next to the round-12 rule alone (--no-purge-disconnect); and the database's own evidence (rows older than the cutoff before and after, retained state rows whose old_state_id the purge set to NULL, statistics_runs)
primary.detection: per arm and monitor, per day and pooled: trials whose target second the verifier flags as attributable at one-second granularity, k of n with the exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval

secondary.suspect_seconds: untouched seconds of the day flagged by a failed keylog range, with the per-row binding and without it (--no-rowbind)
secondary.name_map: every digest transition: changed parts, excused by an operator RENAME marker anchored before it with the new part digests, or unexcused (detected); the verifier's verdict
secondary.restore: segments and keylog ranges the verifier excuses under the RESTORE marker (rule rows_from_the_backup: only segments sealed before the first poll that read the restored recorder and ending after restore point - tol, every row in them an unchanged backup row (key <= the signed backup_wm), every row gone above it; key ranges committed before that poll, rows at or below backup_wm unchanged; E9_IMPL_NOTES.md 11.1; nothing without the operator's RESTORE_DONE within --restore-done-max-s, and no segment starting at or after the hub's start H it carries; a gone row must predate H, a reused-key row must follow it; 12.1), the marker's status (read_back_at, backup_last_key vs the recorder), the archive check in the hub, and any violation outside it
secondary.cost: per day and monitor: per-poll copy or direct read, load, commit, append and total ms (median, p90, max), the read path, failed appends, unobservable polls; seal delay
secondary.quick_check: per day and monitor: the polls at which quick_check was due (seq_local % N == 1, every poll for N = 1), the per-poll snapshot/copy and total cost of those polls against the others, and the polls the monitor's signed records report unobservable, by reason (quick_check_failed, read_raced, after_read, direct_open_failed, file checks)
secondary.bytes: per day and monitor: bytes read and written by the monitor process (/proc/1/io rchar, wchar, read_bytes, write_bytes; sampled every 60 s)
secondary.host: every wall-clock gap above 90 s, every pmset Sleep entry, every jump of the Docker VM's time()-monotonic() offset above 5 s, every hub start with its cause, power source and lid state
secondary.signatures_and_witness: monitor records valid under each monitor's key; markers accepted under the operator's key; chain links, every witnessed head, the final head; anchor refusals by reason
secondary.full_history_seal: seconds holding a row at START without an anchored root (expected 0)

exclusions: only trials whose harness record carries an error are excluded, each counted and listed; a day with a host sleep, a late event or an unplanned hub start is reported with it, not excluded; a night whose purge did not run (database evidence) is reported as such and its marker as unconsumed; if the Mac or Docker restarts, the run stops and the completed days are scored and reported as an incomplete run
known_limits_stated_in_advance: one physical machine: the witnesses run on the Mac outside Docker's VM, a separate trust domain, not a separate party
the attack integrations are installed for each batch; the hub restarts three times a day for them

Home Assistant arms its 04:12 purge on the VM's monotonic clock: a host sleep delays it (the sleep guard restarts the hub at 03:40 if so); a purge delayed past the marker's tolerance can delete rows younger than the scoped cutoff, which then stay unexcused

the restore runs Home Assistant's own restore code at start-up on an archive the operator built from a consistent SQLite copy (Home Assistant's backup manager needs an access token the lab installation does not have)
the person re-link attack is one move of the household account between two persons; E6 measured the effect of a re-link on displayed causes

every recorder snapshot, the restore's backup included, is read OUTSIDE the hub: a throwaway container on the read-only mount of the configuration volume runs SQLite's online backup API from a read-only connection with read-only shared memory (one read transaction, as the direct-read monitor) into the run directory; only if that fails three times does a snapshot go through the hub container's /tmp, recorded per snapshot (event field 'method': readonly_mount or hub_tmp_fallback); the archive is then held outside the hub and checked again inside it, with the hub stopped, before the restore
a declared multi-step change carries one RENAME marker per intermediate state; markers for states no seal caught stay unconsumed on the chain (reported)

a host that withholds or moves markers can turn a benign purge, restore or rename into violations (a false accusation the every-head witness check detects unless the markers were never appended), never a violation into a match (exp/out/e9_dishonest_anchor_markers.json)
backdating by less than about LATE_BOUND plus one poll period is scored as a benign late row; write-time forgery is outside the guarantee
